findings.reason: without an evidence-backed residual demand, the fixed allocation either kills the head arm (blocking the section's closing measure and, through §4, the cached read the plan calls met) or the size must be re-derived from the census, so the node cannot run the clause as written.
findings.text: clause (2) requires "the head arm completes both" the 24-cell and 132-cell cold compiles in one sirius job at `--mem=120G`, while the census the section cites for its "84 percent of the 132-cell read is that call" (job 1338238) records the read's pre-optimization traced value demand as 876.49 GiB at 24 cells and 3,183.55 GiB at 132 cells and places 84% of the module at `polygonanalytic.py:3605`; removing that entire block leaves about 140 GiB at 24 cells and about 509 GiB at 132 cells, four times the job's memory at 24 cells and four times at 132 — and the section records no residual figure for the assembled read

response_events.note: §9 clause 2 now requires the head arm to complete the 24-cell compile in the 120G job; at 132 cells it records completion or the kill with its peak and the largest remaining value family by the census method, which §4's source blocking bounds. Pre-optimization traced totals are not compile peaks (the gradient traces far more than its 28 MB of temporaries), so the clause measures rather than extrapolates.
